item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem: Which of these figures has the largest area?

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: 6 squares arranged in two offset rows of 3]

item.figure_description:
Four shapes composed of identical square units are shown:
- Option A: A rectangle consisting of a grid with 2 rows and 3 columns (6 square units in total).
- Option B: A horizontal bar consisting of a single row of 6 square units (6 square units in total).
- Option C: A rectangle consisting of a grid with 2 rows and 4 columns (8 square units in total).
- Option D: A figure consisting of 6 square units arranged in two rows of 3 squares: a top row of 3 adjacent squares, and a bottom row of 3 adjacent squares shifted to the right so that its leftmost square is directly beneath the rightmost square of the top row (6 square units in total).
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
In this diagram, 2 out of every 3 squares are shaded.

[Image: A rectangle divided into 6 squares]

Which diagram has 3 out of every 4 squares shaded?
reference_items.figure_description:
The stem includes a diagram of a rectangle divided into 2 rows of 3 equal squares (6 squares total). The 4 squares in the first two columns are shaded grey, and the 2 squares in the third column are unshaded (white).

The response options show four diagrams composed of squares:
- Option A: A horizontal row of 3 equal squares, all 3 shaded grey.
- Option B: A horizontal row of 4 equal squares; the first 3 squares are unshaded and the 4th square is shaded grey.
- Option C: A vertical rectangle divided into 4 rows of 2 equal squares (8 squares total). The top 6 squares (3 rows) are shaded grey, and the bottom 2 squares (1 row) are unshaded.
- Option D: A horizontal row of 6 equal squares; the first 3 squares are shaded grey and the last 3 squares are unshaded.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
[Image: a shaded area overlaying a grid made up by small squares with each side of the square measured at 1 cm.]

The squares in the grid above are 1 cm by 1 cm.
What is the shaded area in square centimeters?

Answer: ____ square centimeters

reference_items.figure_description:
A grid of 9 columns and 5 rows of 1 cm by 1 cm squares containing a shaded polygon. Outside the bottom-right corner of the grid, dimension arrows indicate that a single square is 1 cm wide and 1 cm high.

Defining grid coordinates from the top-left corner (0, 0) to the bottom-right corner (9, 5):
- The shaded polygon has vertices at (3, 1), (5, 1), (6, 2), (5, 3), (5, 4), and (3, 4).
- The left side is a vertical line from (3, 1) down to (3, 4), spanning 3 units.
- The bottom side runs horizontally from (3, 4) to (5, 4), spanning 2 units.
- The right side goes vertically up from (5, 4) to (5, 3), 1 unit.
- From (5, 3), a diagonal side goes up and to the right to grid intersection (6, 2).
- From (6, 2), a diagonal side goes up and to the left to grid intersection (5, 1).
- The top side runs horizontally from (5, 1) left to (3, 1), spanning 2 units.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Three arrangements of 3 tiles labeled Rita, Ina, and Lana]

Rita, Ina, and Lana take turns arranging 3 tiles. Each arranges the tiles in a different shape as shown above. Which of the following is true about the area of the shapes?

options.label: A
options.text: Rita’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: B
options.text: Ina’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: C
options.text: Lana’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: D
options.text: All of the shapes have the same area.

reference_items.figure_description:
Three arrangements of three tiles each, labeled "Rita", "Ina", and "Lana":
- Rita: Two squares are placed side by side horizontally, sharing a vertical edge. A triangle sits on top of the left square, with its base along the top edge of that square and its apex pointing upward.
- Ina: A square sits at the top with horizontal top and bottom edges. Attached below it is a triangle sharing the square's bottom horizontal edge and pointing downward. Attached to the lower-right edge of the triangle is a second square, tilted diagonally downward and to the right.
- Lana: Two squares are placed side by side horizontally, sharing a vertical edge. Attached to the right vertical edge of the right square is a triangle pointing to the right.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

- From (3, 5), a horizontal segment runs right 2 units to (5, 5).
The points (5, 1) and (5, 5) are currently open endpoints.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Chris has lots of tiles like this: [Image: Chris's tile]

Julio has lots of tiles like this: [Image: Julio's tile]

Pierre has lots of tiles like this: [Image: Pierre's tile]

Ben has lots of tiles like this: [Image: Ben's tile]

Who would need the least number of tiles to cover a classroom floor with his tiles?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four rectangular/square outlines representing tiles, each shown to the right of a person's name:
- Chris's tile: a medium-small square.
- Julio's tile: a large horizontal rectangle, with both width and area visibly greater than all the other tiles.
- Pierre's tile: a small square, noticeably smaller than Chris's.
- Ben's tile: a medium-large square, larger than Chris's and Pierre's, but smaller in area than Julio's rectangle.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Each figure represents a fraction.

[Image: Four figures labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4]

Which two figures represent the same fraction?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four rectangular figures labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4:
- Figure 1: A rectangle divided vertically into 4 equal strips; the 3 strips on the left are shaded gray, and the 1 strip on the right is unshaded white.
- Figure 2: A rectangle divided into a grid of 2 rows and 4 columns (8 equal parts); the 2 parts in the first column on the left are unshaded white, and the 6 parts in the other 3 columns are shaded gray.
- Figure 3: A rectangle divided vertically into 3 equal strips; the 2 strips on the left are shaded gray, and the 1 strip on the right is unshaded white.
- Figure 4: A rectangle divided into a grid of 2 rows and 2 columns (4 equal parts); the 2 parts in the left column are unshaded white, and the 2 parts in the right column are shaded gray.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Cooney has to form figures 1 to 4 with matches.

Figures 1, 2, and 3 are shown below.

He needs four matches to form figure 1, seven matches to form figure 2, and ten matches to form figure 3.

He uses the same rule each time to make the next figure in the pattern.

[Image: that figure 1 forms a square with four matches, figure 2 forms two squares side by side with seven matches, and figure 3 forms three squares side by side with ten matches.]

How many matches will he need to form figure 4?

Answer: ____

descriptors: [Image: four squares side by side formed with 13 matches.]
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description:
Three figures made of matches arranged in a horizontal row, labeled below with numbers 1, 2, and 3:
- Figure 1: 4 matches arranged to form a single square (one match on each of the four sides).
- Figure 2: 7 matches arranged to form a row of two attached squares side by side, sharing one vertical match in the middle (2 top, 2 bottom, and 3 vertical matches).
- Figure 3: 10 matches arranged to form a row of three attached squares side by side, each adjacent pair sharing a vertical match (3 top, 3 bottom, and 4 vertical matches).

reference_items.stem: In which figure are one-half of the dots black?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four square boxes labeled A, B, C, and D, each containing black (filled) and white (open) circles:
- Option A: Contains 4 circles in a 2 by 2 arrangement. Top row: 1 black circle, 1 white circle. Bottom row: 2 white circles.
- Option B: Contains 6 circles in 2 rows of 3. Top row: white, black, white. Bottom row: black, black, white.
- Option C: Contains 3 circles. Top row: white on the left, black on the right. Bottom row: black on the left.
- Option D: Contains 5 circles arranged in an X pattern like the five dots on a die. Top-left is black, top-right is white, center is white, bottom-left is white, and bottom-right is black.
